issues.legal_issue: Machinery embedded in land is immovable property when the circumstances show it was permanently affixed for the continuing use of an industrial plant.
material_facts: The machinery was embedded in the land to form a fertilizer plant and was used in manufacturing fertilizer.

The nature and arrangement of the machinery, and its description in the conveyance schedule, showed that it was installed permanently to operate the factory rather than to be dismantled and sold as machinery or scrap.
issues.legal_principle: Whether machinery embedded in land is movable or immovable depends on the facts and circumstances, particularly the intention behind its attachment and the purpose for which it was installed. The Court agreed with the High Court’s reliance on Reynolds v. Ashby & Son (1904 AC 466) and Official Liquidator v. Sri Krishna Deo (AIR 1959 All. 247). Sirpur Paper Mills Ltd. v. Collector of Central Excise, Hyderabad (1998 1 SCC 400) did not control because the machinery there was attached for operational efficiency and could be removed for sale, unlike the permanently installed plant here.

predicates.stamp_duty_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the assessment of stamp duty on a conveyance.
predicates.machinery_embedded_in_land: The machinery was fixed or embedded in land.
predicates.permanent_industrial_use_intended: The circumstances show that the machinery was installed to remain in place for the continuing operation of an industrial plant.

issues.definition: When a stamp-duty appeal concerns machinery embedded in land and the circumstances show it was installed for permanent industrial use, the machinery is treated as immovable property.

issues.legal_issue: A conveyance transfers permanently installed plant and machinery when the agreement, conveyance and surrounding circumstances show that the transaction conveyed the industrial business as a going concern together with that property.
material_facts: The sale agreement provided for transfer of the fertilizer business as a going concern and included the land, buildings, plant and machinery for a single slump price.
The conveyance referred to transferring the fertilizer factory and its business as a going concern, and included a schedule plan depicting the factory machinery.
The machinery was not dismantled and separately delivered apart from the land.
The purchaser’s materials submitted to the income-tax authority included the plant and machinery as part of the property being transferred.
issues.conclusion: The conveyance transferred the vendor’s title to the fertilizer business, including the plant and machinery, and their value could be included in determining stamp duty.
issues.legal_principle: The parties’ intention as to what was conveyed must be determined from the conveyance read with the agreement pursuant to which it was executed and the surrounding circumstances. A court may consider prior agreements when determining that intention. Himalaya House Co. Ltd., Bombay v. Chief Controlling Revenue Authority (1972 1 SCC 726) does not establish an absolute bar on considering prior agreements; whether earlier terms are incorporated depends on the facts and the parties’ intention. Under the Stamp Act, the value of property conveyed is relevant to the stamp duty payable.

rule.if: stamp_duty_appeal and transaction_is_business_as_going_concern and agreement_includes_plant_and_machinery and conveyance_and_surrounding_evidence_show_transfer

predicates.stamp_duty_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the assessment of stamp duty on a conveyance.
predicates.transaction_is_business_as_going_concern: The transaction provides for transfer of an operating business as a going concern.
predicates.agreement_includes_plant_and_machinery: The agreement for the transaction includes the plant and machinery among the property to be transferred.
predicates.conveyance_and_surrounding_evidence_show: The conveyance and relevant surrounding evidence indicate that the plant and machinery were included in the transfer.

issues.definition: When a stamp-duty appeal concerns a going-concern business transfer, the agreement includes its plant and machinery, and the conveyance and surrounding evidence indicate their transfer, the plant and machinery are treated as conveyed.

issues.legal_issue: A reviewing court should not disturb a stamp-duty valuation supported by relevant material merely because the Collector reconstituted an enquiry committee, absent demonstrated prejudice or arbitrariness.
material_facts: The Collector first constituted an enquiry committee and later reconstituted it by replacing one member with another official.
The purchaser did not establish that the reconstitution caused prejudice.
The valuation relied on the enquiry committee’s material and reports from technical valuers who considered relevant valuation factors, including the machinery’s life.
The valuations were largely based on documents produced by the purchaser, and the High Court had not treated the valuation as seriously challenged.
issues.conclusion: The Collector was entitled to obtain assistance from an enquiry committee, including a reconstituted committee, and the valuation was not arbitrary or unsupported; the Court declined to interfere with it.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 47-A(2) of the Stamp Act, the Collector may investigate the value of property conveyed and may obtain assistance from available sources, including by constituting or reconstituting an enquiry committee. A valuation is principally a question of fact; a reviewing court will not interfere when it rests on relevant material, absent arbitrariness or demonstrated prejudice. The revision was under Section 56 of the Stamp Act.

rule.if: stamp_duty_appeal and collector_used_valuation_assistance and valuation_based_on_relevant_material and not prejudice_from_committee_change

predicates.stamp_duty_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a stamp-duty valuation of property conveyed.
predicates.collector_used_valuation_assistance: The Collector obtained assistance from an enquiry committee or valuers to assess the property’s value.
predicates.valuation_based_on_relevant_material: The valuation rests on relevant evidence and an explained assessment by suitably informed assessors.
predicates.prejudice_from_committee_change: The party challenging the valuation demonstrated prejudice caused by a change in the composition of the enquiry committee.

issues.definition: In a stamp-duty appeal, a valuation based on relevant material is not disturbed when the Collector used valuation assistance and the challenger did not demonstrate prejudice from a committee change.
